role: Promulgating agency for Average Fuel Economy Standard
stance_basis: agency promulgates and defends the 17.2 mpg fuel economy standard as appropriate and representing maximum feasible average fuel economy
summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is the promulgating agency for the Average Fuel Economy Standard for Nonpassenger Automobiles for Model Year 1979, concluding that 17.2 mpg is the appropriate standard and that a separate 15.8 mpg standard should apply to four-wheel drive recreational vehicles. NHTSA prepared the Final Environmental Impact Statement, analyzing a range of possible standards (16.4–18.7 mpg) and their environmental impacts, and determined the standard represents the maximum feasible average fuel economy for MY 1979. The agency supports the action as beneficial due to significant gasoline savings and relatively minor adverse environmental impacts.
complaint_summary: NHTSA concludes that the appropriate fuel economy standard for nonpassenger automobiles in MY 1979 is 17.2 mpg, with a separate 15.8 mpg standard for four-wheel drive recreational vehicles.

statement.text:
The agency has concluded that the appropriate fuel economy standard for non-passenger automobiles in model year 1979 should be 17.2 mpg. In addition the agency has determined to establish a separate standard of 15.8 mpg for four-wheel drive recreational vehicles and to allow manufacturers of these vehicles the option of meeting this standard or including these vehicles in their total non-passenger automobile fleet and meeting the 17.2 standard on a production weighted basis.
The Average Fuel Economy Standard For Non-passenger Automobiles for Model Year 1979 is attached to this statement and presents the resolution of other issues which were outstanding at the time of preparation of this report.
